name: SwipeableRow
description: A list row that slides sideways to show actions behind it, such as archive or delete. Swiping is a shortcut: the same actions are reachable with a button and the keyboard, so nobody depends on the gesture. Actions can sit on either side, can be turned off per person, and the row stays scrollable up and down.

children.description: The row's content. It sits on an opaque surface that covers the actions until it is moved. Put any buttons or links the row needs inside it as usual.

startActions.description: Actions behind the start of the row, revealed by swiping toward the end: { id, label, icon?, tone?, onAction, permission? }. Keep to one to three. tone is "default", "primary" or "danger". An action may carry a permission ("allow", "disabled", "hidden" or { state, reason }): hidden actions are not drawn; disabled ones stay as focusable, inactive buttons with the reason read out.

endActions.description: Actions behind the end of the row, revealed by swiping toward the start. Same shape as startActions. Reading direction is followed, so in a right-to-left page the sides swap with the text.

actionsLabel.description: Accessible name of the button that shows the actions without a swipe, and of the group of actions. Name the row in it: "Actions for invoice 1042".

open.description: Which side is open, to control it. Pass null to keep the row closed. Use with onOpenChange. Leave it out to let the row manage itself.

defaultOpen.description: Which side starts open when you do not control it.

onOpenChange.description: Called with the side that is now open, or null when the row closed.

fullSwipe.description: A long swipe, past most of the row's width, runs the first action of that side and closes the row. Use it only for actions that are easy to undo: archive, not delete.

closeOnAction.description: Close the row after an action runs.

isDisabled.description: Turn swiping off. The actions stay reachable with the button and the keyboard.

classNames.description: Class names for the parts, by slot name, added after the built-in ones. Slots: root, content, actions, action, toggle.

keyboard: Tab: reaches the row's own controls, then the actions button
Enter or Space on the actions button: shows the actions and moves focus to the first one
Tab and Shift+Tab move between the actions; Enter or Space runs one
Escape: closes the row and returns focus to the actions button
requirements: Swiping is never the only way: a button shows the same actions, reachable by keyboard and screen reader
The actions button has a name, says whether the actions are shown (aria-expanded) and is revealed on focus so keyboard users see it
Actions that are not shown are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree
The actions are a named group of real buttons, each with a text label; an icon is never the only name
A disabled action stays focusable (aria-disabled), does nothing and says why
A swipe does not trigger a click on what was under the finger, and a tap on an open row closes it instead of activating it
Vertical scrolling still works over the row; only a horizontal move starts the swipe
Each action is at least 80 CSS pixels wide and as tall as the row
A long swipe that runs an action is off unless fullSwipe is set, and is meant for undoable actions
The slide is turned off when the user prefers reduced motion
screenReader: "Actions for invoice 1042, button, collapsed"; after it is pressed, "expanded" and the group "Actions for invoice 1042" with its buttons: "Archive, button", "Delete, button"

use_when: Lists of messages, tasks or records on a phone where each row has one to three quick actions
Actions people repeat often and want near their thumb
avoid_when: A row with many actions: use a menu button in the row
A destructive action with no confirmation or undo
Wide screens with a mouse: show the actions as buttons or a menu in the row
anti_patterns: Making the swipe the only way to reach an action: the actions button must stay available
Using fullSwipe for delete without an undo
More than three actions behind a row: they will not fit and cannot be told apart
Putting a horizontal scroller inside a row: the two gestures fight
UI permission is not security: hiding or disabling an action only changes what people see, so the server must check access again for every request
